readings.title: The Appointed Times
readings.subtitle: The Weekly Sabbath
readings.text: [Leviticus 23:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [2] <dq>“Speak to the children of Yisra’ĕl, and say to them, ‘The appointed times of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, which you are to proclaim as set-apart gatherings, <dn>My</dn> appointed times, are these:</dq> [3] <dq>‘Six days work is done, but the seventh day is a Sabbath of rest, a set-apart gathering. You do no work, it is a Sabbath to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> in all your dwellings.</dq> [4] <dq>‘These are the appointed times of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, set-apart gatherings which you are to proclaim at their appointed times.</dq>

readings.title: The Spring Feasts
readings.subtitle: Passover and Unleavened Bread
readings.text: [Leviticus 23:5] <dq>‘In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, between the evenings, is the Passover to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [6] <dq>‘And on the fifteenth day of this month is the Festival of Unleavened Bread to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> – seven days you eat unleavened bread.</dq> [7] <dq>‘On the first day you have a set-apart gathering, you do no servile work.</dq> [8] <dq>‘And you shall bring an offering made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for seven days. On the seventh day is a set-apart gathering, you do no servile work.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: The Harvest of Barley
readings.subtitle: The First-Fruits
readings.text: [Leviticus 23:9] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [10] <dq>“Speak to the children of Yisra’ĕl, and you shall say to them, ‘When you come into the land which <dn>I</dn> give you, and shall reap <dn>את</dn> its harvest, then you shall bring a sheaf of the first-fruits of your harvest to the priest.</dq> [11] <dq>‘And he shall wave <dn>את</dn> the sheaf before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for your acceptance. On the morrow after the Sabbath the priest waves it.</dq> [12] <dq>‘And on that day when you wave the sheaf, you shall prepare a male lamb a year old, a perfect one, as a burnt offering to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>,</dq> [13] <dq>and its grain offering: two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil, an offering made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, a sweet fragrance, and its drink offering: one-fourth of a hin of wine.</dq> [14] <dq>‘And you do not eat bread or roasted grain or fresh grain until the same day that you have brought an offering to your <dn>Elohim</dn> – a law forever throughout your generations in all your dwellings.</dq>

readings.title: The Harvest of Wheat
readings.subtitle: The Feast of Weeks (Shavuot)
readings.text: [Leviticus 23:15] <dq>‘And from the morrow after the Sabbath, from the day that you brought the sheaf of the wave offering, you shall count for yourselves: seven completed Sabbaths.</dq> [16] <dq>‘Until the morrow after the seventh Sabbath you count fifty days, then you shall bring a new grain offering to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [17] <dq>‘Bring from your dwellings for a wave offering two loaves of bread, of two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour they are, baked with leaven, first-fruits to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [18] <dq>‘And besides the bread, you shall bring seven lambs a year old, perfect ones, and one young bull and two rams. They are a burnt offering to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, with their grain offering and their drink offerings, an offering made by fire for a sweet fragrance to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [19] <dq>‘And you shall offer one male goat as a sin offering, and two male lambs a year old, as a peace offering.</dq> [20] <dq>‘And the priest shall wave <dn>את</dn> them with the bread of the first-fruits as a wave offering before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, with the two lambs. They are set-apart to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for the priest.</dq> [21] <dq>‘And on this same day you shall proclaim a set-apart gathering for yourselves, you do no servile work – a law forever in all your dwellings throughout your generations.</dq> [22] <dq>‘And when you reap <dn>את</dn> the harvest of your land do not completely reap the corners of your field when you reap, and do not gather any gleaning of your harvest. Leave them for the poor and for the stranger. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: The Fall Feasts
readings.subtitle: The Day of Trumpets (Yom Teruah)
readings.text: [Leviticus 23:23] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [24] <dq>“Speak to the children of Yisra’ĕl, saying, ‘In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, you have a rest, a remembrance of blowing of trumpets, a set-apart gathering.</dq> [25] <dq>‘You do no servile work, and you shall bring an offering made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.’ ”</dq>

readings.title: The Day of Atonement
readings.subtitle: Yom Kippur
readings.text: [Leviticus 23:26] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [27] <dq>“On the tenth day of this seventh month is the Day of Atonement. It shall be a set-apart gathering for you. And you shall afflict <dn>את</dn> your beings, and shall bring an offering made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [28] <dq>“And you do no work on that same day, for it is the Day of Atonement, to make atonement for you before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq> [29] <dq>“For any being who is not afflicted on that same day, he shall be cut off from his people.</dq> [30] <dq>“And any being who does any work on that same day, that being <dn>I</dn> shall destroy from the midst of his people.</dq> [31] <dq>“You do no work – a law forever throughout your generations in all your dwellings.</dq> [32] <dq>“It is a Sabbath of rest to you, and you shall afflict <dn>את</dn> your beings. On the ninth day of the month at evening, from evening to evening, you observe <dn>את</dn> your Sabbath.”</dq>

readings.title: The Feast of Booths
readings.subtitle: Sukkot
readings.text: [Leviticus 23:33] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [34] <dq>“Speak to the children of Yisra’ĕl, saying, ‘On the fifteenth day of this seventh month is the Festival of Booths for seven days to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [35] <dq>‘On the first day is a set-apart gathering, you do no servile work.</dq> [36] <dq>‘For seven days you bring an offering made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. On the eighth day there shall be a set-apart gathering for you, and you shall bring an offering made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. It is a closing festival, you do no servile work.</dq> [37] <dq>‘These are the appointed times of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> which you proclaim as set-apart gatherings, to bring an offering made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, a burnt offering and a grain offering, a slaughtering and drink offerings, as commanded for every day,</dq> [38] <dq>besides the Sabbaths of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and besides your gifts, and besides all your vows, and besides all your voluntary offerings which you give to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [39] <dq>‘On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, when you have gathered in <dn>את</dn> the fruit of the land, you celebrate <dn>את</dn> the festival of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for seven days. On the first day is a rest, and on the eighth day a rest.</dq> [40] <dq>‘And you shall take for yourselves on the first day the fruit of good trees, branches of palm trees, twigs of leafy trees, and willows of the stream, and shall rejoice before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn> for seven days.</dq> [41] <dq>‘And you shall celebrate <dn>את</dn> it as a festival to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> for seven days in the year – a law forever in your generations. Celebrate it in the seventh month.</dq> [42] <dq>‘Dwell in booths for seven days; all who are native born in Yisra’ĕl dwell in booths,</dq> [43] <dq>so that your generations know that <dn>I</dn> made <dn>את</dn> the children of Yisra’ĕl dwell in booths when <dn>I</dn> brought <dn>את</dn> them out of the land of Mitsrayim. <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.’ ”</dq> [44] Thus did Mosheh speak of <dn>את</dn> the appointed times of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> to the children of Yisra’ĕl.

readings.title: The Light and The Bread
readings.subtitle: Perpetual Ordinance for the Tabernacle
readings.text: [Leviticus 24:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [2] <dq>“Command <dn>את</dn> the children of Yisra’ĕl that they bring to you clear oil of pressed olives for the light, to make the lamps burn continually.</dq> [3] <dq>“Outside the veil of the Witness, in the Tent of Meeting, Aharon is to arrange <dn>את</dn> it from evening until morning before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> continually – a law forever throughout your generations.</dq> [4] <dq>“He is to arrange <dn>את</dn> the lamps on the clean lampstand before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> continually.</dq> [5] <dq>“And you shall take fine flour and bake twelve cakes with it, two-tenths of an ephah in each cake.</dq> [6] <dq>“And you shall set <dn>את</dn> them in two rows, six in a row, on the clean table before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [7] <dq>“And you shall put pure frankincense on each row, and it shall be on the bread for a remembrance portion, an offering made by fire to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [8] <dq>“On every Sabbath he is to arrange it before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> continually, from the children of Yisra’ĕl – an everlasting covenant.</dq> [9] <dq>“And it shall be for Aharon and his sons, and they shall eat it in a set-apart place, for it is most set-apart to him from the offerings of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> made by fire – a law forever.”</dq>

readings.title: Justice for Blasphemy
readings.subtitle: The Law applies to Native and Stranger
readings.text: [Leviticus 24:10] And the son of an Yisra’ĕlite woman, whose father was a Mitsrite, went out among the children of Yisra’ĕl. And the Yisra’ĕlite woman’s son and a man of Yisra’ĕl strove in the camp. [11] And the Yisra’ĕlite woman’s son blasphemed <dn>את</dn> the Name, and cursed. So they brought <dn>את</dn> him to Mosheh. Now his mother’s name was Shelomith the daughter of Diḇri, of the tribe of Dan. [12] And they placed him in ward, to declare to them the mouth of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. [13] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh, saying, [14] <dq>“Bring <dn>את</dn> the one who has cursed outside the camp, and all who heard him shall lay <dn>את</dn> their hands on his head, and all the congregation shall stone <dn>את</dn> him.</dq> [15] <dq>“And speak to the children of Yisra’ĕl, saying, ‘Anyone who curses his <dn>Elohim</dn> shall bear his sin.</dq> [16] <dq>‘And he who blasphemes the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall certainly be put to death, and all the congregation shall certainly stone him, the stranger as well as the native. When he blasphemes the Name, he is put to death.</dq> [17] <dq>‘And a man who strikes any being of man dead shall certainly be put to death.</dq> [18] <dq>‘And he who strikes a beast dead pays for it, body for body.</dq> [19] <dq>‘And if a man causes a blemish in his neighbour, as he has done so it is done to him:</dq> [20] <dq>fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth. As he has caused a blemish in a man, so it is done to him.</dq> [21] <dq>‘And he who strikes a beast dead pays for it, but he who strikes a man dead is put to death.</dq> [22] <dq>‘You are to have one right-ruling, for the stranger and for the native, for <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.’ ”</dq> [23] And Mosheh spoke to the children of Yisra’ĕl, and they brought <dn>את</dn> the one who cursed outside the camp and stoned <dn>את</dn> him with stones. And the children of Yisra’ĕl did as <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> commanded <dn>את</dn> Mosheh.

readings.title: The Sabbath of the Land
readings.subtitle: The Shemittah Year
readings.text: [Leviticus 25:1] And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> spoke to Mosheh on Mount Sinai, saying, [2] <dq>“Speak to the children of Yisra’ĕl, and say to them, ‘When you come into the land which <dn>I</dn> give you, then the land shall observe a Sabbath to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.</dq> [3] <dq>‘Six years you sow <dn>את</dn> your field, and six years you prune <dn>את</dn> your vineyard, and gather in <dn>את</dn> its fruit,</dq> [4] <dq>but in the seventh year the land is to have a Sabbath of rest, a Sabbath to <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. Do not sow <dn>את</dn> your field and do not prune <dn>את</dn> your vineyard.</dq> [5] <dq>‘Do not reap <dn>את</dn> what grows of its own of your harvest, and do not gather <dn>את</dn> the grapes of your unpruned vine, for it is a year of rest for the land.</dq> [6] <dq>‘And the Sabbath of the land shall be to you for food, for you and your servant, and for your female servant and your hired servant, and for the stranger who sojourns with you,</dq> [7] <dq>and for your livestock and the beasts that are in your land. All its increase is for food.</dq>

readings.title: The Year of Jubilee
readings.subtitle: Liberty Throughout the Land
readings.text: [Leviticus 25:8] <dq>‘And you shall count seven Sabbaths of years for yourself, seven times seven years. And the time of the seven Sabbaths of years shall be to you forty-nine years.</dq> [9] <dq>‘Then you shall cause the trumpet of the Jubilee to sound on the tenth day of the seventh month; on the Day of Atonement you cause the trumpet to sound through all your land.</dq> [10] <dq>‘And you shall set <dn>את</dn> the fiftieth year apart, and proclaim release throughout all the land to all its inhabitants, it is a Jubilee for you. And each of you shall return to his possession, and each of you return to his clan.</dq> [11] <dq>‘That fiftieth year is a Jubilee to you. Do not sow, nor reap <dn>את</dn> what grows of its own, nor gather from <dn>את</dn> its unpruned vine.</dq> [12] <dq>‘For it is a Jubilee, it is set-apart to you. Eat <dn>את</dn> its increase from the field.</dq> [13] <dq>‘In this Year of Jubilee, let each one of you return to his possession.</dq> [14] <dq>‘And when you sell any property to your neighbour or buy from the hand of your neighbour, do not take advantage of one another.</dq> [15] <dq>‘According to the number of years after the Jubilee you buy from your neighbour, and according to the number of years of crops he sells to you.</dq> [16] <dq>‘According to the greater number of years you increase its price, and according to the fewer number of years you diminish its price, because he sells to you according to the number of the years of the crops.</dq> [17] <dq>‘And do not oppress one another, but you shall fear your <dn>Elohim</dn>. For <dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> your <dn>Elohim</dn>.</dq> [18] <dq>‘And you shall do <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> laws and guard <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> right-rulings, and do <dn>את</dn> them. And you shall dwell in the land in safety.</dq> [19] <dq>‘And the land shall yield <dn>את</dn> its fruit, and you shall eat to satisfaction, and dwell there in safety.</dq> [20] <dq>‘And since you might say, “What do we eat in the seventh year, since we do not sow nor gather in <dn>את</dn> our increase?”</dq> [21] <dq>‘Therefore <dn>I</dn> have commanded <dn>את</dn> <dn>My</dn> blessing on you in the sixth year, and it shall bring forth <dn>את</dn> the crop for three years.</dq> [22] <dq>‘And you shall sow <dn>את</dn> the eighth year, and eat old food from the crop, until the ninth year. Until its crop comes in, you eat the old food.</dq> [23] <dq>‘And the land is not sold beyond reclaim, for the land is <dn>Mine</dn>, for you are strangers and sojourners with <dn>Me</dn>.’ ”</dq>
